summary: Turn 14. All prior candidates are explained and pending_work was empty (the snapshot metadata confirms this is an autonomous audit of upstream swiftpaxos at commit 35c69365), so I targeted a deterministic durability defect that can later be executed. Sourced finding: recordInstanceMetadata (epaxos/epaxos.go:199-215) allocates a 9+r.N*4 byte record and writes inst.bal into b[0:4], then writes inst.vbal into the same b[0:4] (lines 205-206), so the bal field is overwritten by vbal and the ballot is never persisted; status, seq and deps are written correctly. Map additions (base version set to the accepted 4): B-DURABLE-META (A6) describing the write and F-DURABLE-META asserting that the record encodes bal, vbal, status, seq and deps, with an explicit cross_activity_effects entry to A2 because the persisted ballot is the per-instance authority context recovery compares against; the previously 'deferred' surface for epaxos.Replica.recordInstanceMetadata/recordCommands/sync is now mapped to that behavior with its reason updated, and the matching map_changes clarification is supplied. New source S-DURABLE-META covers epaxos/epaxos.go:199-215. Submitted action=continue with a Candidate (disposition concrete_suspicion, preferred_check direct_test, priority 2; activity_classes A6 with supported core activity A2; principal fact F-DURABLE-META, direct behavior B-DURABLE-META, supporting B-PROPOSE and B-RECOVERY-START; obligation_relation_kind preservation). Its question asks whether the metadata write persists bal as intended given that bal and vbal share one offset, so a durable record cannot distinguish the ballot from the pre-accept ballot. Counterevidence keeps it honest (Durable is false by default, and no replay reader exists in the captured files) and unknowns state the two open premises: whether a requirement exists that the record round-trip bal and vbal separately, and whether any restart path reads it. This Candidate is the closest so far to a deterministic unit check: with Durable=true and a buffer StableStore the emitted bytes can be compared against the fields written. Preflight validation returns valid=true; formal acceptance and any execution remain the controller's.
